nodes.label: FairShare
nodes.rationale: Web app that makes group grades match who actually did the work, by making effort visible rather than punishing anyone.

nodes.label: Social Loafing
nodes.rationale: People exert less effort in a group than alone. This is the core problem FairShare exists to counter; documented by Latane, Williams & Harkins (1979).

nodes.label: Ringelmann Effect
nodes.rationale: Older finding that per-person effort drops as group size grows; the basis social loafing builds on.

nodes.label: Peer Assessment
nodes.rationale: Teammates rating each other is shown to be fair and accurate vs teacher marks (Falchikov & Goldfinch 2000). Justifies FairShare's private peer-review mechanism.

nodes.label: CATME
nodes.rationale: Existing college peer-evaluation tool; FairShare adapts the same idea to be free and student-run with no teacher account.
